articles.title: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
articles.titleEn: Tracing the spread of Celtic languages using ancient genomics
articles.abstract: Celtic languages are today restricted to Europe’s Atlantic fringes but were widely spoken across the continent during the Iron Age 1–3 . How Celtic achieved this early distribution remains contested 4 , with alternative archaeological and linguistic models proposing different homelands and dispersal routes. Here we analyse genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which these models fit reconstructed demographic histories. We identify three main processes shaping European population structure that are relevant to the Celtic dispersal. First, the arrival of Steppe-related ancestry with Bell Beaker-associated groups after around 4400 bp (calibrated years before present or 1950 ce ) across the region in which Celtic and related languages were later spoken. Second, a movement from southwestern Europe into Britain during the Bronze Age (3800–3200 bp ), consistent with scenarios in which Celtic formed along the Atlantic façade. Third, a westward expansion of ancestry related to Late Bronze Age Knovíz–Urnfield-associated populations from eastern central Europe (3200–2800 bp ), affecting France, the British Isles, northeastern Iberia and Italy and later associated with Iron Age Hallstatt and La Tène contexts 5–8 . Although all three movements have parallels with proposed models, we argue that the final movement, from eastern central Europe, is most parsimonious for the spread of Celtic. Although human history does not necessarily follow a parsimonious trajectory 9 and language shifts need not track genetic change, these results delimit the demographic scenarios that are plausible for the emergence of Celtic in prehistoric Europe.

articles.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
articles.titleEn: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
articles.abstract: Hydrogen-bearing materials are central to low-carbon energy technologies 1 , but hydrogen itself is difficult to detect and localize at the nanoscale 2–6 . This hinders the development of advanced materials with better efficiency. Atom probe tomography (APT) can map hydrogen in three dimensions and at high resolution, yet characterization of dilute, mobile, interstitial hydrogen in metals has remained challenging because of low solubility, the ambiguity owing to hydrogen trapping by structural defects, as well as the artefacts introduced during hydrogen introduction 4–6 . Here we address whether interstitial hydrogen in solution in materials can be distinguished from defect-trapped hydrogen in APT. Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, together with face-centred cubic (FCC) multi-principal-element alloys (MPEAs) containing coherent FCC precipitates, we show that deuterium atoms reproducibly concentrate in hydrogen-affinitive phases in a manner consistent with theoretical predictions. We further resolve differences in deuterium content between phases with distinct local chemistries and crystal structures, consistent with their different calculated hydrogen solution energies. These findings demonstrate that APT can move beyond identifying hydrides and solute-decorated defects to examine hydrogen in solid solution, providing new insights into hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys and informing materials design for hydrogen-related applications.

articles.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
articles.titleEn: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is highly heritable, and mutations in hundreds of genes have been implicated as individually rare causes of ASD 1–3 . Understanding how disruptions to these functionally diverse genes lead to the core features of ASD remains a major challenge 4 . Moreover, ASD is three- to four-fold more common in male than in female individuals 5 , and female autistic people tend to carry more autosomal risk alleles for ASD compared with their male counterparts 6,7 ; however, the biological basis of this ‘female protective effect’ (FPE) has remained unknown 8,9 . Here we show that individual perturbations of 18 ASD genes in human neural progenitor cells converge on shared effects on gene expression, including widespread downregulation of other ASD genes. De novo reconstruction of a gene regulatory network enabled identification of central transcriptional regulators that drive this transcriptomic convergence, including prominent ASD gene CHD8 and candidates including REST . Furthermore, X-linked transcription factor ZFX, which is expressed from both the active and the inactive X chromosomes in female individuals 10 , emerged as a key activator of many ASD genes: we propose that the higher ZFX expression level observed in the female brain can buffer damaging mutations in diverse ASD genes, contributing to the female protective effect. Together, these results show how key gene regulatory networks can become broadly and similarly dysregulated upon disruption of individual ASD genes and provide molecular insight into the female protective effect in ASD.

articles.title: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
articles.titleEn: Venousization enables angiogenesis in the absence of VEGFR signalling
articles.abstract: The vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) ligand and its main receptor VEGFR2 are considered to be essential for endothelial differentiation, proliferation, sprouting and survival 1 . Blood vessels cannot form in growing embryos or tissues when VEGF–VEGFR2 signalling is compromised in all cells 2,3 . The anti-VEGF antibody, which can block angiogenesis in cancer, wound healing or ischaemic diseases, is among the most widely used antibodies in the clinic. However, vascular resistance to anti-VEGF therapy has been reported 4,5 . Here we used iFlpMosaics and iSuRe –HadCre to induce and track genetic mosaics of endothelial cells (ECs) lacking VEGFR2 during the entire embryonic and postnatal development. These Vegfr2 -knockout ( Vegfr2 KO ) ECs adapted, proliferated normally and competed with wild-type cells over time, eventually forming a substantial portion of the vascular network in most organs. Vegfr2 KO ECs could not sprout during the first wave of angiogenesis in most tissues, because this process is highly VEGF-dependent and favours growth and mobilization of wild-type ECs. However, owing to their inability to respond to VEGF, Vegfr2 KO ECs became dominant in veins, which represented a long-term and continuous source of ECs for subsequent waves of VEGF-independent angiogenesis. Comparative single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of ECs with acute and long-term loss of VEGFR2 identified both common and organ-specific molecular mechanisms of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss. These included significant endothelial venousization and upregulation of ligands for VEGFR1 and VEGFR3. VEGFR1 only partially compensated for VEGFR2 loss in capillary ECs, whereas VEGFR3 compensated only in arterial ECs. Loss of the three VEGF receptors did not compromise venous growth. Notably, loss of the master regulator of venous development, NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), significantly compromised expansion of Vegfr2 KO ECs. This work has implications for our understanding of the role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and demonstrates venousization as a mechanism of adaptation and resistance to VEGF signalling loss during angiogenesis.

articles.title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
articles.titleEn: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
articles.abstract: Exoplanet imaging is the main method for detailed characterization of planets orbiting beyond 1 au (ref. 1 ) but it requires suppressing the bright glare of the star to see the faint planet light. As well as sophisticated instrumentation 2,3 , effective image processing is necessary for starlight suppression, which continues to be a substantial limitation 4 . Standard algorithms use reference images for starlight modelling and thus they are limited by inevitable telescope instabilities that change from reference to science observation 5,6 . Addressing this challenge will increase the number of planets amenable to direct imaging and will be a notable step towards imaging exo-Earths with future observatories 7 . Here we present a new physics-based method for starlight subtraction. Our method combines a multistep optimization with a flexible physical model to produce a starlight model, allowing modelling and compensation of instrument instabilities. We use automatic differentiation (autodiff) 8 to optimize millions of model parameters. We demonstrate our method on observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) Near-InfraRed Camera (NIRCam) 9–11 coronagraph instrument. We achieve sensitivity 2–15 times superior to standard techniques, including the first detection of 51 Eridani b (ref. 12 ) at 4.3 μm. This is the first time, to our knowledge, that such an approach has demonstrated substantially improved sensitivity on real, on-sky coronagraphic imaging. Our framework can be extended to other current and future ground-based and space-based observatories, including the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope and the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), potentially relaxing the unprecedented stability requirements needed to make these a success.

articles.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
articles.titleEn: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
articles.abstract: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent nondetections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of nonradiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intracluster medium composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20 to 30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.

articles.title: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy
articles.titleEn: Comprehensive classification of HCN1 variants linked to neurodevelopmental disorders with and without epilepsy
articles.abstract: Hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated 1 (HCN1) channels mediate the cationic I h current, a fundamental regulator of neuronal excitability and synaptic integration, and are predominantly expressed in the cortex and hippocampus. Although HCN1 variants have been increasingly identified in patients with epilepsy, from milder forms to developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEE), genotype–phenotype correlations remain poorly defined. Here, we used patch-clamp electrophysiology and confocal imaging in HEK293 cells to functionally characterize 43 HCN1 variants identified in patients with neurodevelopmental disorders, with or without epilepsy. Based on biophysical properties, we established a classification system comprising four distinct functional classes: I) low or no current; II) hyperpolarizing shift in voltage dependence; III) depolarizing shift in voltage dependence; and IV) generation of an instantaneous current. The molecular basis for this classification was further interpreted using available cryo-EM structures of HCN1. Integration with clinical data from 50 patients revealed a striking correlation between functional class and clinical presentation. Loss-of-function variants prevailed among individuals with milder phenotypes or without epilepsy, with the latter distinctively clustering within the channel selectivity filter. In contrast, gain-of-function and mixed variants were predominantly associated with DEE. Finally, we demonstrate that allosteric modulators, including peptides NB6 and TRIP8b nano and the small molecule J&J12e, effectively normalize channel function across three of the four classes in vitro. These findings establish a biophysical framework for interpreting HCN1 variants, demonstrating that the direction of channel dysfunction is a major determinant of epilepsy risk and severity, and providing a conceptual foundation for future class-based precision medicine approaches.

articles.title: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
articles.titleEn: Progressive shifts in soil respiration response to long-term nitrogen enrichment across global forests and grasslands
articles.abstract: Soil stores the largest pool of actively cycling carbon (C) on land, and its dynamics under global changes are critical for projecting climate feedbacks. Global nitrogen (N) deposition has more than doubled since the 1860s; however, the temporal dynamics of soil C emissions under prolonged N deposition are poorly understood. Here, using a global time-series dataset compiled from 38 long-term experiments in forests and grasslands, we find that the response of soil respiration (Rs) to N addition systematically shifts from a transient increase persisting for approximately 2 y to a sustained suppression over time (mean effect = −6%; 95% CI = [−10%, −3%]). Rs in forests and grasslands followed consistent nonlinear trajectories, characterized by a rapid initial decline in the magnitude of the response, which progressively leveled off. Notably, suppression of Rs emerged when cumulative N inputs exceeded a threshold of ~100 kg N ha −1 . Consequently, the suppression was both stronger and occurred more rapidly under high-level N additions (>50 kg N ha −1 y −1 ). These temporal dynamics were associated with N-induced soil acidification and related changes in microbial properties. Overall, these findings indicate that accurate prediction of land–atmosphere C fluxes under global change requires models to capture the reported temporal dynamics.

articles.title: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
articles.titleEn: Lead impairs long-term memory by disrupting mitochondrial redox homeostasis in Drosophila
articles.abstract: Lead (Pb) exposure remains a major environmental risk factor for cognitive dysfunction, yet the cellular mechanisms underlying Pb-induced memory impairment are poorly understood. Here, we show that both developmental and adult-onset Pb exposure selectively disrupts protein-synthesis-dependent long-term memory (LTM) in Drosophila melanogaster while sparing other memory forms. Using a mitochondria-targeted redox biosensor (mito-roGFP2-Orp1), we found that Pb elevates mitochondrial oxidative stress and disrupts redox homeostasis in cholinergic neurons and in dorsal-anterior-lateral (DAL) neurons, a critical locus for LTM consolidation. Pb-induced redox imbalance suppresses training-induced de novo protein synthesis in DAL neurons, thereby impairing memory consolidation. Antioxidant treatment with epigallocatechin gallate restores mitochondrial redox balance and rescues LTM by reinstating activity-dependent protein synthesis in DAL neurons. These findings identify mitochondrial redox dysregulation as a key mechanism linking environmental Pb exposure to impaired memory consolidation. Our results further establish a genetically tractable platform for dissecting neurotoxic mechanisms and for evaluating antioxidant-based strategies to mitigate Pb-induced cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
articles.titleEn: Municipal sludge disposal emerges as a major, hidden, and rapidly growing atmospheric mercury source
articles.abstract: Wastewater treatment greatly reduces mercury pollution in aquatic ecosystems but does not eliminate it. Here, we identify municipal sludge disposal as a major, long-overlooked atmospheric mercury source. In China, sludge disposal emitted 42 - 10 + 18 Mg in 2024, exceeding 10% of national anthropogenic emissions and ranking third after cement production and nonferrous metal smelting. These emissions have increased by nearly a thousandfold since the 1970s and are concentrated in densely populated urban areas, driven by the rapid expansion of sludge incineration, codisposal, and composting. Our findings reveal a cross-media pollution transfer embedded in sustainability transitions and call for sludge disposal to be incorporated into UNEP mercury budget and Minamata Convention assessments.

articles.title: A tetravalent bispecific protein enables targeted degradation of VCAM-1 and VEGFR for treatment of choroidal neovascularization
articles.titleEn: A tetravalent bispecific protein enables targeted degradation of VCAM-1 and VEGFR for treatment of choroidal neovascularization
articles.abstract: Wet age-related macular degeneration (AMD), a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, is driven by pathological choroidal neovascularization (CNV). Although anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) therapies remain the clinical standard, their utility is constrained by incomplete responses in nearly 50% of patients and off-target risks—such as geographic atrophy—stemming from non-specific VEGF blockade. Here, we identify a robust correlation between vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1) and VEGF/VEGF receptor (VEGFR) expression in aqueous humor from AMD patients and in murine CNV models. Thus, we engineered a tetravalent bispecific protein, RHV, by functionalizing an L-rhamnulose-1-phosphate aldolase scaffold with peptides that selectively bind VCAM-1 and the VEGFR on neovessels. The tetravalent design confers high apparent affinity, enhancing pathological endothelial targeting while sparing healthy retinal vasculature. RHV induces concurrent internalization and lysosomal degradation of both VCAM-1 and VEGFR via a head-to-tail binding mode, leading to sustained inhibition of the VEGF/VEGFR, PI3K/AKT and Apelin/APJ signaling pathways. In murine CNV models, a single intravitreal injection of RHV exhibits superior ocular retention and lesion penetration, achieving therapeutic efficacy comparable to aflibercept [a ligand-trap fusion protein for VEGF-A, VEGF-B and placental growth factor (PIGF)] at one-quarter of the molar dose. This dual-receptor degradation-based strategy represents a targeted and durable approach for treating ocular neovascularization.

articles.title: Entropic tightening of knots in granular chains under vibration
articles.titleEn: Entropic tightening of knots in granular chains under vibration
articles.abstract: Knots are common in long chains, from DNA and proteins to everyday strings, yet direct observation of knot dynamics is difficult. Using granular chains on vibrating platforms, we directly visualize knot dynamics and find that knot cores spontaneously tighten, a behavior observed across different knot types. We quantitatively explain spontaneous knot tightening using knot-tube theory: segments confined within the knot core experience entropic loss and tend to escape the core to gain conformational entropy. Although driven granular chains are not in thermodynamic equilibrium, their steady-state knot-size statistics are approximately captured by equilibrium statistical mechanics and Monte Carlo simulations. Analyses of state-transition probabilities and time-reversal asymmetry suggest a weak violation of detailed balance when the granular dynamics are projected onto the knot-size coordinate. Finally, we discuss the possible relevance of knot tightening to topoisomerase-mediated DNA unknotting.

articles.title: Amphipathic helices repurpose a Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter to function at Plasmodium –erythrocyte membrane contact sites
articles.titleEn: Amphipathic helices repurpose a Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter to function at Plasmodium –erythrocyte membrane contact sites
articles.abstract: The interface between the malaria parasite Plasmodium spp. and its host erythrocyte critically mediates nutrient uptake, lipid exchange, and protein export required for parasite replication and thus pathogenesis. Approximately half of this interface consists of narrow membrane contact sites, a region defined by only 3 to 4 nm of aqueous space between the parasite plasma membrane and the parasitophorous vacuole membrane. Despite its extent, the region remains largely uncharacterized and inaccessible, not least due to its narrowness. The sole identified resident is the Plasmodium falciparum Niemann-Pick Type C1-Related protein, PfNCR1, an essential Patched/NPC1-like cholesterol transporter, suggesting this conserved transporter family has evolved an unconventional adaptation for localizing to membrane contact sites that can reveal a mechanism to access the region. Here, using live-cell microscopy and assessment of cholesterol homeostasis, we identify a helix–linker–helix (HLH) domain as the necessary modification for efficient PfNCR1 localization. We find that correct localization is required for the parasite to maintain low cholesterol levels, connecting targeting to function. Using a glycosylphosphatidylinositol-anchored fluorescent reporter as a minimal membrane-associated protein, we show that the HLH domain is sufficient to drive localization to the narrow membrane contact site region. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that targeting depends on the physicochemical character of the targeting domain rather than a specific primary sequence, identifying amphipathicity as a determining property of the HLH domain. Taken together, we propose physicochemical partitioning as a fundamental principle for protein targeting at the Plasmodium –erythrocyte interface, and for driving direct functional interactions of a Patched/NPC1-like protein with a second membrane.

articles.title: Revealing the Mechanism of Solute Anomalous Transport Within Discrete Fracture Networks: Insight From Differences in Flow Pathways
articles.titleEn: Revealing the Mechanism of Solute Anomalous Transport Within Discrete Fracture Networks: Insight From Differences in Flow Pathways
articles.abstract: Understanding anomalous solute transport is crucial for effective groundwater contamination prediction and control, and efficient utilization of subsurface oil reservoirs. Variations in fracture pathways within fractured rock masses play a pivotal role in these anomalous behaviors. Traditional models face challenges in capturing complex phenomena, such as early breakthrough, heavy tailing, and multimodality, caused by these variations, highlighting the need for a quantitative, pathway‐resolved understanding of fracture‐network transport responses. In this study, a three‐dimensional discrete fracture network model was constructed from measured fracture data and subsequently converted into an equivalent pipe network for efficient simulation of both flow and solute transport. By identifying complete inlet‐to‐outlet flow pathways and tracing particle trajectories to these pathways, the study quantified the contributions of different pathways to solute transport behaviors. The results show that early arrivals are concentrated in a small number of connected pathways, whereas late arrivals are associated with longer, lower‐velocity connected pathways that contribute to power‐law tailing; parallel pathway groups with substantially different travel times contribute to multimodal behavior. Furthermore, the early breakthrough index ( I EA ) and tailing index ( β BTC ) show systematic correspondence with flow‐conditioned pathway travel‐time characteristics across 200 network realizations. Including variable apertures correlated with trace length further enhances flow focusing, early breakthrough, and tailing. These findings demonstrate that pathway decomposition provides a quantitative means of attributing breakthrough‐curve features to identifiable transport pathways, offering a path‐resolved interpretation of anomalous transport arising from differential advection and hydrodynamic dispersion in complex fracture networks.

articles.title: Atmospheric Stilling Reshapes Algal Blooms and Eutrophication Risk in Shallow Lakes
articles.titleEn: Atmospheric Stilling Reshapes Algal Blooms and Eutrophication Risk in Shallow Lakes
articles.abstract: Atmospheric stilling, defined as long‐term decline in wind speed, has emerged as a widespread climate signal, yet its role as an independent driver of eutrophication in shallow lakes remains poorly understood. Taking Lake Taihu as a representative case, we applied a coupled hydrodynamic‐ecological model (GOTM‐WET) to quantitatively estimate the impacts of declining wind speed on a large shallow lake, while keeping external nutrient loading constant. Model simulations showed that under a strong stilling scenario (45% wind reduction relative to the 2018–2022 baseline), mean surface water temperature increased by 1.96°C, while weakened vertical mixing reduced oxygen transport to bottom waters, resulting in a 56.2% decline in bottom‐water dissolved oxygen (DO). The development of hypoxic conditions intensified sediment anaerobic processes, enhancing internal phosphorus release while simultaneously accelerating denitrification‐driven nitrogen loss. These coupled biogeochemical responses drove a shift toward a phosphorus‐enriched and nitrogen‐depleted nutrient regime, fundamentally altering nutrient limitation patterns. Consequently, surface chlorophyll a (Chl a ) concentrations increased markedly, particularly in summer, with a mean enhancement of 45.4%, accompanied by more persistent and intense algal blooms, indicating pronounced seasonal differences in lake ecosystem responses to declining wind speed. Our results demonstrate that declining wind speeds modulate lake hydrodynamics, oxygen supply, and nutrient structure, driving coupled responses in lake temperature‐nutrient‐phytoplankton systems and markedly increasing the risk of eutrophication, highlighting atmospheric stilling as a previously underappreciated driver of the eutrophication risk in large shallow lakes under future climate change.

articles.title: Continental water storage trends and budgets from the GRACE/GRACE-FO Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P)
articles.titleEn: Continental water storage trends and budgets from the GRACE/GRACE-FO Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P)
articles.abstract: The Global Gravity-based Groundwater Product (G3P) provides global groundwater storage (GWS) variations derived from GRACE/GRACE-FO terrestrial water storage (TWS) change by subtracting root-zone soil moisture, glacier mass change, surface water storage, and snow water equivalent. G3P thus provides the first globally consistent, publicly available groundwater dataset from satellite gravimetry for continental-scale water resources assessment. Here, we use G3P to assess global GWS trends over the extended GRACE/GRACE-FO record, jointly with TWS and the subtracted storage components. A central challenge is that apparent long-term trends in GRACE/GRACE-FO water storage records can reflect persistent storage change, natural climate variability, hydrological memory, and observational errors, complicating trend detection and continental-scale storage-change budgets. We address this using a calibrated trend-analysis framework that jointly accounts for trend, seasonal, and stochastic variations in each grid-cell time series. Statistically significant trends are then aggregated to quantify volumetric GWS and TWS gains, losses, and net changes at continental and global scales. Applying this framework to 21.5 years of data (April 2002–September 2023), we find that groundwater depletion is a major contributor to freshwater decline at continental scales, most prominently in Asia (−55 km 3 yr −1 ), while cryospheric mass loss dominates the strongest TWS declines in high-latitude and glacierized regions. Pronounced regional contrasts include increasing groundwater storage across large parts of Africa (+37 km 3 yr −1 ), negative trends in drought-affected regions, and widespread negative or near-threshold GWS tendencies across the Northern Hemisphere. Globally, significance-filtered net GWS and TWS changes are approximately −27 and −183 km 3 yr −1 , respectively. The corresponding gross negative GWS change of approximately 103 km 3 yr −1 is of the same order as model-based estimates of global groundwater depletion. Sensitivity tests indicate robust results: at 95 %, detected area increases by 30 % for TWS and 36 % for GWS, while net-loss magnitudes rise by only 9 % and 18 %. Across much of the seasonal-to-interannual spectral range, GWS is the dominant individual storage-component signal within TWS, which highlights the importance of groundwater for continental freshwater availability.

articles.title: Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO v1.0) for explicit discrete-slope control in terrain preprocessing: a case study with WRF-ARW (v4.6.1)
articles.titleEn: Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO v1.0) for explicit discrete-slope control in terrain preprocessing: a case study with WRF-ARW (v4.6.1)
articles.abstract: Kilometre-scale Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) simulations over terrain with steep slopes often require strong smoothing to prevent numerical instability, but conventional domain-wide filters alter terrain at every grid point, regardless of whether local slopes require reduction. Slope-Constrained Orography (SCO) is an offline terrain preprocessing method that prescribes a target slope angle θ and adjusts only those grid points whose eight-neighbour elevation differences exceed the implied bound, leaving the remaining terrain unchanged. By prescribing the slope constraint directly, SCO provides a geometrically interpretable primary user-facing parameter for terrain construction and stability testing. In a 1 km WRF case over the highly complex terrain of the southeastern Tibetan Plateau, the least-modified stable SCO member among those tested modifies 14 % of points with a mean elevation change of 8.2 m, compared with 100 % modification and 108.1 m for the corresponding WRF Preprocessing System (WPS) member. The successful SCO configuration produces lower near-surface wind and temperature errors in this case.

articles.title: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
articles.titleEn: GECKO-A v1.0: exploring VOC oxidation trajectories through comparison with the master chemical mechanism
articles.abstract: Numerical models are crucial tools for understanding complex chemical systems such as the atmosphere, and their sensitivity across a range of conditions. In atmospheric chemistry models, reaction mechanisms are used to represent chemical transformations and define the underlying system of equations. Building highly explicit mechanisms that capture the full complexity of organic oxidation occurring in the atmosphere remains challenging owing to the large number of intermediates involved, the breadth of reaction pathways, and the limited availability of reliable kinetic and thermodynamic data. The Generator for Explicit Chemistry and Kinetics of Organics in the Atmosphere (GECKO-A) was developed to address these limitations by enabling the systematic construction of near-explicit mechanisms. Here, we present its first open-source release (v1.0), which incorporates updated chemical protocols and structure-activity relationships, together with its companion box model for mechanism integration. GECKO-A's performance is benchmarked through systematic comparisons with the Master Chemical Mechanism (MCM v3.3.1), based on simulations of the oxidation of five representative hydrocarbons (butane, octane, dodecane, toluene, and α -pinene) under environmental conditions ranging from urban to remote. The two approaches yield similar oxidation pathways for small and structurally simple compounds. However, differences increase with the size and complexity of the carbon backbone. In particular, the simplifications inherent to the MCM tend to limit the formation of multifunctional products and promote earlier fragmentation, resulting in notable discrepancies in the predicted volatility of secondary organic carbon and, consequently, in secondary organic aerosol yields. These discrepancies stem from how each mechanism treats multigenerational oxidation. The two approaches remain similar for early-generation products, but diverge as later generations become predominant. This divergence also extends to the water solubility of secondary organic carbon, and to its partitioning into aqueous condensed phases. GECKO-A also enables mechanism generation at different levels of chemical resolution. A reduced mechanism, denoted red-GECKO-A, is compared to the high-resolution mechanism used throughout this study. It closely reproduces the simulated oxidative trajectories for most parent compounds and scenarios. Discrepancies emerge for octane and dodecane under NO x -poor conditions.

articles.title: Hybrid implicit–explicit XFEM simulation of injection-induced seismicity: resolving multi-scale rupture nucleation and dynamics
articles.titleEn: Hybrid implicit–explicit XFEM simulation of injection-induced seismicity: resolving multi-scale rupture nucleation and dynamics
articles.abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid implicit–explicit time-integration strategy for simulating injection-induced fault reactivation within a fully coupled poroelastodynamic extended finite element (XFEM) framework. Modeling these systems is inherently challenging due to the extreme separation of temporal scales – ranging from hours to days for fluid diffusion to milliseconds for dynamic rupture. Although the fully implicit formulation can provide enhanced numerical stability, stability alone does not guarantee sufficient temporal accuracy during nonlinear fault rupture. The results demonstrate close agreement between simulations with minimum time-step sizes of 10 −5 and 10 −6 s for the investigated slip and event-scale observables on the adopted spatial mesh, indicating temporal convergence for these quantities at 10 −5 s. This time-step size is substantially smaller than the mesh-based explicit stability estimate. To reduce computational cost, the proposed strategy employs an implicit solver for quasi-static loading and nucleation and switches to a central-difference-based mechanical solver with implicit pressure integration once a prescribed slip-velocity threshold is exceeded. At a switching threshold of 0.01 m s −1 , the hybrid simulation requires approximately 10.0 h, compared with 26.4 h for the fully implicit reference, corresponding to a computational-time reduction of 62.12 %. The hybrid strategy reproduces the overall rupture sequence, stress evolution, final accumulated fault slip, and seismic moment. However, differences remain in the timing and magnitude of peak slip velocities, rupture-propagation speeds, and transient particle motion. These findings demonstrate the computational potential of the hybrid formulation for the investigated two-dimensional configuration, while highlighting the need for further assessment of transient dynamic accuracy and computational performance across different spatial discretizations and geological conditions.

articles.titleEn: Rethinking the Role of Cattle in Wetlands: An Underexplored Dimension of Biodiversity Connectivity

articles.title: Resolving the Multiple Controls of Biomass Production Efficiency in Woody Plants
articles.titleEn: Resolving the Multiple Controls of Biomass Production Efficiency in Woody Plants
articles.abstract: Plants assimilate carbon through photosynthesis to support biomass production (BP), autotrophic respiration ( R a ) and the synthesis of non‐structural compounds. Biomass production efficiency (BPE), the fraction of assimilated carbon allocated to BP, is one key factor influencing ecosystems' potential to store carbon. However, there is no consensus on the controls of BPE, and even the sign of its response to growth temperature is unclear. By means of statistical hypothesis testing using the largest observational dataset to date on annual BPE ( n = 514 records) from evergreen and deciduous woody plants, we confirm earlier findings that BPE declines with stand age and is greater in deciduous plants. However, we also show that BPE declines toward more organic, sandy, or alkaline soils and increases with climatic aridity, while declining with warmer growing seasons and increasing with warmer winters. Such a dual temperature response is consistent with additional carbon costs due to the need for cold‐hardening processes, and reconciles contradictory published reports of both positive and negative effects of temperature on BPE. Notably, our analysis provides novel evidence that BPE is significantly higher in species associated with arbuscular mycorrhizal (AM) fungi than in those associated with ectomycorrhizal (EcM) fungi and mixed EcM–AM associations. Our analysis explains the observed BPE patterns better than dynamic global vegetation models (DGVMs) from the TRENDY (Trends and Drivers of the Regional‐Scale Terrestrial Sources and Sinks of Carbon Dioxide) project, which show a weaker correspondence with observations. In particular, our model captures reduced BPE in boreal regions, consistent with the predominance of ectomycorrhizal (EcM) species there. This study advances understanding of the global controls of BPE, and suggests a route toward the improved representation of plant growth in vegetation and land surface models.

articles.title: Embracing the Heterogeneity Within Particulate and Mineral‐Associated Organic Matter for the Next Generation of Soil Carbon Questions
articles.titleEn: Embracing the Heterogeneity Within Particulate and Mineral‐Associated Organic Matter for the Next Generation of Soil Carbon Questions
articles.abstract: Soil organic matter (SOM) is a complex and dynamic substrate central to the functioning of terrestrial ecosystems. Because of its heterogeneity, SOM is routinely parsed into physical fractions with more uniform composition and behavior. Over the last several years, particulate (POM) and mineral‐associated (MAOM) organic matter have become the most widely adopted of these fractions, which has given the field a shared, comparable framework for resolving the first‐order heterogeneity within SOM. As fractionation has become routine, however, it has become clear that POM and MAOM identity alone cannot resolve the finer, second‐order variation that additional mechanistic inference requires. This is in part because the fractions are operationally defined composites, whose properties vary across composition, formation pathway, and behavior. Conceptualizing them as the terminal state of analysis collapses each fraction to its central tendency, flattening the distribution and obscuring the structure on which more complex questions depend. Here we propose embracing this within‐fraction heterogeneity rather than averaging over it, treating POM and MAOM as composite distributions whose internal structure underlies the variation in how they form, persist, and function. We suggest that this view can be operationalized via two complementary approaches: tailoring fractionation methods to target subpopulations most relevant to a question, and pairing fractions with orthogonal measurements. Together, these resolve the within‐fraction distribution that bulk measurements integrate over, narrowing the analysis onto the most explanatory slice of the bulk SOM. Similar to the original framework, we do not aim to prescribe a certain methodology, but rather a way of thinking about heterogeneity within SOM, in which a separation is justified by the understanding it produces rather than the data it generates. This way of reasoning allows POM and MAOM to continue linking organic matter to its functions, and in doing so supports more informed stewardship of soil carbon.

articles.title: Enhanced weathering of glacial rock flour drives coupled inorganic and organic carbon sequestration in a five-year field experiment
articles.titleEn: Enhanced weathering of glacial rock flour drives coupled inorganic and organic carbon sequestration in a five-year field experiment
articles.abstract: Enhanced rock weathering (ERW) has been proposed as a scalable carbon dioxide removal strategy, yet long-term field-based constraints on weathering rates and associated carbon sequestration remain limited. Here, we present a 5-year field assessment of Greenlandic glacial rock flour (GRF) applied at 50 t ha −1 to a sandy agricultural soil in Denmark. Using a soil mass balance approach, based on depletion of Mg which provided the most tightly constrained weathering signal, we estimate that at least 56 % of the applied GRF dissolved over 5 years. Initial uptake of CO 2 via ERW is estimated at 3.2–4.9 t CO 2 ha −1 when accounting for carbonate speciation in the acidic soil solution, with the potential for further gains if complete downstream transport of weathering products and subsequent re-equilibration with the more alkaline marine carbonate system is assumed. In addition to inorganic carbon removal, GRF-treated plots exhibited significantly higher soil organic carbon stocks, equivalent to the storage of an additional 18.3 t CO 2 ha −1 . These results demonstrate substantial weathering and carbon sequestration over 5 years under field conditions in a temperate climate and suggest that both inorganic and organic carbon dynamics contribute meaningfully to the overall climate impact of ERW of GRF. The findings provide rare multi-year field constraints on ERW performance and underscore the importance of robust measurements for quantifying carbon removal in agricultural systems, representing the first implementation of mass balance methods within the framework of a randomized block design.

Using a soil mass balance approach, based on depletion of Mg which provided the most tightly constrained weathering signal, we estimate that at least 56 % of the applied GRF dissolved over 5 years. Initial uptake of CO 2 via ERW is estimated at 3.2–4.9 t CO 2 ha −1 when accounting for carbonate speciation in the acidic soil solution, with the potential for further gains if complete downstream transport of weathering products and subsequent re-equilibration with the more alkaline marine carbonate system is assumed. In addition to inorganic carbon removal, GRF-treated plots exhibited significantly higher soil organic carbon stocks, equivalent to the storage of an additional 18.3 t CO 2 ha −1 . These results demonstrate substantial weathering and carbon sequestration over 5 years under field conditions in a temperate climate and suggest that both inorganic and organic carbon dynamics contribute meaningfully to the overall climate impact of ERW of GRF. The findings provide rare multi-year field constraints on ERW performance and underscore the importance of robust measurements for quantifying carbon removal in agricultural systems, representing the first implementation of mass balance methods within the framework of a randomized block design.

articles.title: Unreported mass movement cascades and future Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) hazard in Jammu and Kashmir, Western Himalaya
articles.titleEn: Unreported mass movement cascades and future Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) hazard in Jammu and Kashmir, Western Himalaya
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: The Warwan sub-basin in Jammu and Kashmir is a remote glaciated region containing several glacial lakes and has recently experienced population growth and infrastructure development. Due to inaccessibility and geomorphic masking, multiple mass movement events, including avalanches and glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), have remained largely unreported. This study analyzes three major avalanche events from the past two decades. The September 2005 and September 2020 avalanches originated from glaciers GL-B and GL-A within the same glacier complex, while the March 2020 rock–ice avalanche initiated from the headwall of glacier GL-F in an adjacent valley and terminated before reaching its ablation zone. Runout mapping shows that the September 2020 avalanche descended from the headwall of GL-A and impacted its proglacial lake, triggering a GLOF. In contrast, the September 2005 event terminated before reaching the glacial lake that began forming in 1999 at the terminus of GL-B. Geomorphic analysis indicates persistent sediment influx from meltwater streams of GL-D and GL-E into the lake associated with GL-A, progressively infilling the lake. Continued glacier retreat caused meltwater to accumulate behind the sediment infill, dividing the lake into two disconnected lakes. Impact from the September 2020 avalanche led to complete drainage of stored water and sediment, generating a downstream debris flow. Pre- and post-GLOF imagery reveal breaching and widening of the outflow channel and deposition of a debris fan downstream. The repeated history of mass movements and continued growth of glacial lakes raise serious hazard concerns in the Warwan sub-basin. GLOF modeling identifies Lake-B as a potentially hazardous lake in its present condition, posing significant downstream risk. Settlements such as Youdu and Qaderna, along with bridges, roads, and residential structures, lie within potential GLOF inundation zones. High sediment availability from past mobilization and deposition along the valley increases the potential of debris-flow cascades, posing elevated risks to downstream infrastructure and hydropower, underscoring the need for preparedness and mitigation planning. GLOF modeling suggests that an early warning system closer to the source will be able to provide a good lead time in case of potential GLOFs in the valley.

articles.title: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
articles.titleEn: Nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement of tetrasubstituted alkenes enables divergent access to fused δ-lactams
articles.abstract: Transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer has emerged as a powerful strategy for alkene functionalization, yet its application to sterically congested tetrasubstituted alkenes remains severely underdeveloped. Here, we report an Ir(III)-catalyzed nitrene-triggered aziridination–rearrangement cascade that enables the efficient conversion of cyclic-substituted tetrasubstituted alkenes into cycloalkane-fused δ-lactams. The transformation proceeds under mild conditions with excellent yields and uniformly high diastereoselectivities and exhibits broad compatibility with carbon-, oxygen-, and nitrogen-based nucleophiles, including structurally complex and biologically relevant substrates. Combined experimental and computational studies support a concerted aziridination by an Ir–nitrenoid to generate a strained tricyclic intermediate, which undergoes a strain-release-driven aza-semipinacol rearrangement to furnish a bicyclic azacarbocation. Divergent nucleophilic interception or elimination of this intermediate provides rapid access to structurally diverse fused δ-lactam architectures. These findings establish a nitrene-triggered carbocationic rearrangement manifold for the functionalization of tetrasubstituted alkenes and expand the synthetic potential of transition-metal-catalyzed nitrene transfer.

articles.titleEn: Seagrass sediment organic carbon burial rates are globally significant
articles.abstract: Crucial for coastal carbon sequestration, global seagrass organic carbon (OC) burial rates remain uncertain as early estimates were derived from mixed methodologies across geographically and taxonomically biased datasets. Here, we present a data-driven reassessment from a synthesis of 332 sediment cores spanning the last century. Results show that seagrasses bury OC at 25 ± 3 g OC m −2 yr −1 (geometric mean), with an area-weighted global average of 33 ± 9 g OC m −2 yr −1 . Based on a revised mapped seagrass extent (247,700–366,400 km 2 ), global burial scales to 6–15 Tg C yr −1 . articles.title: A Prospective Cooling Machine for the Svalbard Branch of Norwegian Atlantic Water in a Future Climate
articles.titleEn: A Prospective Cooling Machine for the Svalbard Branch of Norwegian Atlantic Water in a Future Climate
articles.abstract: The evolution of air‐sea interaction and the ocean north of Svalbard is investigated using a high‐resolution configuration of the coupled climate model HadGEM3‐GC3.1 under a high‐emission pathway (SSP5‐8.5). To the west and north of Svalbard, where the West Spitsbergen Current—the northward branch of the Norwegian Atlantic Current—carries warm and saline Atlantic Water (AW) into the Arctic, we identify a significant shift in the pattern of sea‐ice decline. In the late 20th century, the sea‐ice edge retreats gradually downstream along the current's pathway. However, in the 21st century, the ice edge retreats northward across the continental slope, leading to the simultaneous exposure of the AW core to the atmosphere. This rapid increased exposure triggers enhanced cooling and convective mixing along the AW pathway. The water column undergoes destratification due to the AW encroachment, along with mixing, resulting in a warmer and less stratified upper ocean downstream on this pathway. The potential temperature maximum of the AW shoals, increasing the potential for enhanced oceanic heat loss. A closed regional ocean heat content analysis reveals that net advective heat convergence into the region increases substantially, driving a sustained wintertime surface heat loss that stabilizes at ∼70 TW by the 2040 s. These changes suggest that a prospective “cooling machine” north of Svalbard will soon emerge in a future climate, operating at a capacity comparable to the Barents Sea and fundamentally altering the water mass transformation and heat export into the deep Arctic interior.

articles.title: Vanishing Winters and Shrinking Ice: Ecosystem Services and Societal Impacts in the Laurentian Great Lakes
articles.titleEn: Vanishing Winters and Shrinking Ice: Ecosystem Services and Societal Impacts in the Laurentian Great Lakes
articles.abstract: The Laurentian Great Lakes are undergoing rapid winter transformations, with profound implications for human societies. Winter air temperatures have increased, accelerating ice loss since the mid‐1990s. These trends are altering thermal regimes, shifting precipitation from snow to rain, and increasing winter runoff and nutrient fluxes, with cascading effects across physical, chemical, and biological systems. Using the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment framework, we synthesize how warming winters affect supporting, regulating, provisioning, and cultural ecosystem services, as well as their positive and negative socioeconomic implications for the Sustainable Development Goals. Winter warming is altering supporting services by reducing the stability and extent of under‐ice habitats that provide refugia for biodiversity and disrupting nutrient cycling. Regulating services are also affected, through increased greenhouse gas emissions, shoreline erosion and flooding, altered disease dynamics and changes in lake‐effect snowfall. Provisioning services, such as freshwater supply and fisheries, are increasingly vulnerable to harmful algal blooms, infrastructure disruptions, and reduced habitat for cold‐water species. Cultural and recreational activities including ice fishing, Indigenous traditions, and winter tourism are also threatened, while unstable ice may increase drowning risks. Although reduced ice cover may benefit navigation and summer recreation, these gains are outweighed by broader ecological and cultural losses. Collectively, these findings show that lake ice functions as a mediating variable regulating interconnected ecological and societal processes. Its loss threatens ecosystem resilience and heightens socioeconomic vulnerabilities for the 40 million people who depend on the Great Lakes. Addressing these challenges will require cross‐border cooperation.

articles.titleEn: Prediction of Escaped Powerline‐Caused Fires in Alberta, Canada
articles.abstract: Powerlines have increasingly become a source of wildfire ignitions, contributing to more escaped and catastrophic fires during extreme fire weather. articles.title: Integration of Aerosol–Cloud Interactions With a Land‐Atmosphere Coupled Model in the Gray Zone
articles.titleEn: Integration of Aerosol–Cloud Interactions With a Land‐Atmosphere Coupled Model in the Gray Zone
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Clouds strongly impact net surface radiation, creating differential heating patterns, and trigger land breezes that in turn organize cloud development. These dial processes determine the location of persistent ecohydrological regimes at local scales. Aerosol–cloud interactions (ACI) directly impact the diurnal cycle of cloud optical depth, and therefore the surface energy budget; yet they are generally not explicitly represented in studies of land‐atmosphere interactions. To address this gap, a 3D Large‐Eddy Simulation model was modified to describe ACI in the gray zone. The goal is to simulate realistic cumulus cloud dynamics consistent with the spatial dynamics of land surface moisture and temperature, and associated boundary layer processes. The model is tested and evaluated using simulations at hectometer resolution with prescribed diurnal surface heating corresponding to idealized wet (low Bowen ratio [LBR]) and dry (high Bowen ratio [HBR]) surface boundary conditions. Expected cloud sensitivity is well captured: compared to LBR, HBR clouds have a significantly higher cloud base (about 1 km), up to 50% reduction in total cloud fraction, and cloudiness ends earlier by about 2 hr due to enhanced turbulence and lower moisture availability. Analyses of the evolution of 3D cloud drop size distributions show that the model captures the cloud life cycle, including aerosol activation, condensational growth, enhanced collision‐coalescence, and aerosol regeneration. The results show that resolved eddy‐scale (sub‐km) within‐cloud circulations modulate cloud microphysical structure by locally altering supersaturation at minute timescales. Successive aerosol regeneration yields coarser cloud condensation nuclei, producing a coarse‐aerosol mode, and impacting mid‐day cloud fraction and cloudiness persistence.

articles.title: Advancing Satellite Solar‐Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence Data Assimilation in Land Surface Models: An Assessment Over Boreal Evergreen Needleleaf Forests
articles.titleEn: Advancing Satellite Solar‐Induced Chlorophyll Fluorescence Data Assimilation in Land Surface Models: An Assessment Over Boreal Evergreen Needleleaf Forests
articles.journal: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
articles.abstract: Boreal forests represent about 20% of the global forest carbon sink and contribute to climate change mitigation, yet land surface models (LSMs) struggle to simulate their gross primary production (GPP). Space‐borne observations of solar‐induced fluorescence (SIF) have been used to improve LSM GPP through data assimilation. However, previous work has shown that assimilating SIF alone can degrade GPP for some vegetation types, highlighting the need for enhanced process representation and tightly constrained parameters. Uncertainties in the representation of non‐photochemical quenching (NPQ), which regulates the SIF‐GPP relationship, further complicate this challenge. Here, we develop a data assimilation strategy to assess the complementarity of satellite SIF from TROPOMI and in situ GPP in constraining GPP dynamics simulated by the ORCHIDEE LSM over boreal evergreen needleleaf forests. We evaluate this framework using two NPQ schemes, a process‐based formulation separating sustained and reversible components, and a generic model representing total NPQ. After assimilation, evaluation against independent SIF grid cells and flux sites shows improved seasonal cycles of both SIF and GPP. Regional‐scale simulations better match independent GPP products (FLUXSAT and FLUXCOM‐X‐BASE) over 2001–2020, with over 77% RMSD reduction in the mean seasonal cycle versus the prior, largely reflecting the recalibration of model parameters after implementation of the new radiative transfer scheme. SIF‐GPP co‐assimilation outperforms GPP‐only assimilation for the GPP latitudinal profile, and also for the GPP mean seasonal cycle in three out of four cases. Although the two NPQ models affect the simulated SIF seasonal cycle differently, their performances after assimilation are similar.

articles.title: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
articles.titleEn: Zero emissions commitment depends on warming level
articles.abstract: When anthropogenic CO 2 emissions cease, global temperature does not stabilize immediately. The resulting global temperature change, the zero emissions commitment, is central to carbon budget assessments and understanding reversibility of global warming, yet its dependence on prior warming levels remains unclear. Here we show, using zero-emission simulations with the UK Earth System Model (UKESM1.2) across global warming levels of 1.5–5 K, that the zero emissions commitment stays near zero up to 2 K but becomes positive at higher warming levels, reaching 0.4–0.6 K after ~ 150 years. This dependence indicates that stabilizing or reversing warming becomes progressively more difficult as peak temperature rises. We identify the mechanism behind this behaviour: stronger warming from higher radiative disequilibrium and weakening carbon sinks, driven by saturated land carbon uptake and the reduced radiative impact of CO 2 drawdown at higher background CO 2 concentrations. Higher peak warming therefore commits the planet to additional warming, limiting temperature-overshoot reversibility.

articles.title: Thermodynamic stabilization of substrate protein within the GroEL:ES chaperonin cage
articles.titleEn: Thermodynamic stabilization of substrate protein within the GroEL:ES chaperonin cage
articles.abstract: The adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-regulated GroEL/ES chaperonin of Escherichia coli promotes protein folding by transiently encapsulating unfolded substrate protein in a nano-cage formed by the cylindrical GroEL and the lid-shaped GroES. How this confinement modulates the folding energy landscape, allowing accelerated protein folding unimpaired by aggregation, remains incompletely understood. Prompted by recent observations suggesting that the chaperonin cavity may favor unfolding [I. Korobko et al. , Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A. 119 , e2213170119 (2022)], here we reinvestigated the effect of encapsulation on protein thermodynamic stability. To allow thermal unfolding of an encapsulated substrate protein, we generated a destabilized variant of maltose-binding protein (MBP) by introducing four mutations, quadruple mutant-MBP (QM-MBP), lowering the melting temperature ( T m ) from 63.6 °C to 44.3 °C. GroEL/ES accelerated the slow spontaneous folding of QM-MBP ~20-fold. The protein reached a native-like structure while encapsulated inside GroEL:ES, as demonstrated using hydrogen/deuterium exchange and single molecule fluorescence resonance energy transfer analyses in presence and absence of the ligand maltose. Importantly, confinement in the thermally stable chaperonin shifted the cooperative unfolding transition of QM-MBP to a T m of 52.4 °C, corresponding to a stabilization by 4.6 kcal mol −1 . In-cage thermal unfolding was reversible, indicating that the environment of the chaperonin cavity is conducive to folding. These findings suggest that a thermodynamically stabilizing effect of the GroEL:ES cage contributes to promoting protein folding.

articles.title: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
articles.titleEn: Coacervate droplets as a liquefier for the solid-to-liquid transition of RNA aggregates
articles.abstract: Biomolecular condensates are functionally gated by their material properties. While RNA is a primary structural scaffold, its sequence-specific interactions can aberrantly drive condensates into dysfunctional solid aggregates. Yet, actively reversing this solidification to restore function remains a fundamental challenge, impeding progress in synthetic biology and therapeutics interventions. Here, we establish that complex coacervates can be engineered as liquefiers to actively remodel solid RNA–peptide aggregates into functional liquid droplets. Integrating systematic experiments with all-atom simulations, we decode a multiscale mechanism: coacervate infiltration at the micrometer scale mediates molecular buffering at the nanometer scale, which fluidizes the crosslinked network to drive macroscopic liquefaction. articles.title: Assessing the Effects of Climate Change Projections on Water Fluxes and Streamwater NO 3 –N in Lowland Catchments Using Isotope‐Aided Water Quality Modeling
articles.titleEn: Assessing the Effects of Climate Change Projections on Water Fluxes and Streamwater NO 3 –N in Lowland Catchments Using Isotope‐Aided Water Quality Modeling
articles.abstract: Understanding how climate change alters hydrological connectivity and associated nitrate dynamics remains a key challenge in lowland, mixed land‐use catchments. Here, we use a tracer‐aided, fully distributed ecohydrological modeling framework to investigate how future climate conditions may influence water fluxes and nitrate dynamics in such systems, using the Demnitzer Mill Creek catchment in Germany as an exemplar. To provide mechanistic insight into hydrological transport and biogeochemical processing, we applied diagnostic metrics based on water age and the Damköhler (Da) number, which links water residence times with reaction timescales. Results indicate that projected warming and a shift of precipitation toward winter progressively strengthen hydrological connectivity, leading to increased infiltration, evapotranspiration, and subsurface flow contributions. This stronger connectivity reorganizes nitrate transport across the catchment, with enhanced lateral redistribution, declining agricultural soil nitrate stocks, and lower stream nitrate concentrations. At the same time, processing times decrease more strongly than hydrological exposure times, increasing Da number and indicating a shift toward stronger reaction dominance. Uncertainty arises from climate forcing projections, simplified representations of subsurface processes, and assumptions regarding future agricultural practices. Overall, the results highlight the coupled role of transport and processing of nutrients and the value of coupled tracer‐aided water quality models. The findings also emphasize hydrological connectivity as a key control on future water quality.

articles.title: Quantifying Ion‐Specific Effects on the Size‐Exclusion Transport of Multi‐Sized Colloids in Porous Media Using a Novel Synthetic DNA Labeling Approach
articles.titleEn: Quantifying Ion‐Specific Effects on the Size‐Exclusion Transport of Multi‐Sized Colloids in Porous Media Using a Novel Synthetic DNA Labeling Approach
articles.abstract: Colloids strongly adsorb pollutants and promote their co‐transport in aquatic environments, posing substantial ecological contamination risks. However, quantifying the size exclusion effect (SEE), a critical mechanism that enhances colloid transport, remains challenging in multi‐sized colloid systems, owing to limited high‐resolution labeling methods and ion‐induced dynamic aggregation. Here, we developed a high‐resolution DNA‐based tracing framework that employs synthetic DNA fragments to individually label multi‐sized colloids (0.1, 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 μm), and utilizes quantitative real‐time PCR (qPCR) to quantify their transport behavior in saturated quartz sand under the typical environmental ions (NaCl/CaCl 2 ). The results demonstrated that Ca 2+ promoted colloid aggregation and retention more strongly than Na + , thereby modifying size‐exclusion behavior, although the magnitude of SEE depended on colloid size and transport conditions. While the SEE generally exhibited a positive size dependence in the single‐sized system, the multi‐sized system exhibited higher SEE for 0.1 and 0.2 μm colloids relative to their single‐sized counterparts under certain solution chemistry conditions. This discrepancy may be attributed to pore blockage caused by larger colloids within the multi‐sized system. Furthermore, two transport patterns, blocking and ripening, were identified from the breakthrough curves of DNA‐labeled colloids. Correlation analysis revealed that the SEE parameter ( γ ) was positively correlated with the normalized retention parameter ( S max / C 0 ) under blocking conditions ( r = 0.655). This study highlights the effectiveness of synthetic DNA labeling approach in tracking the transport of multi‐sized colloids, providing new insights into the fate of colloids in natural and engineered porous systems.

articles.title: Merging Regional Climate Models and Remote Sensing Observations to Better Estimate Mountain Snow Water Equivalent
articles.titleEn: Merging Regional Climate Models and Remote Sensing Observations to Better Estimate Mountain Snow Water Equivalent
articles.abstract: Large‐scale, high‐resolution estimation of snow water equivalent (SWE) in mountainous regions remains challenging. Continental‐scale approaches, including SWE reconstruction and regional climate model (RCM) simulations, are computationally expensive at high resolutions. We present Blender, a variational data assimilation method that improves modeled SWE and snowfall time series by modifying snowpack mass and energy balance while minimizing changes to input precipitation and energy fluxes, subject to remotely sensed snow cover fraction constraints. Blender combines the advantages of RCM simulation and SWE reconstruction and can be applied as a post‐processing step to many gridded snow data sets. We tested Blender at 500 m resolution in the Tuolumne watershed, Sierra Nevada, USA, during water years 2013, 2016, and 2017 (low, average, and high snow accumulation). We tested Blender with prior inputs from an RCM and ERA5‐Land (ERA5L), and evaluated posterior (output) performance using 18 Airborne Snow Observatory (ASO) flights, and compared its performance with the Western United States Snow Reanalysis (WUS‐SR). Blender improved spatial SWE patterns relative to ASO in all years for the RCM prior (RMSEP: 17.2% → 11.5%, R : 0.39 → 0.72) and ERA5L prior (RMSEP: 13.9% → 12.9%, R : 0.003 → 0.59), approaching WUS‐SR performance (RMSEP = 9.5%, R = 0.82). Blender improved snow water storage (SWS) estimates for the RCM prior but not for ERA5L prior, although ERA5L posterior SWS remained reasonably accurate (median absolute error of 27%). Blender provides a flexible and efficient pathway toward higher‐resolution, large‐scale SWE estimation in mountainous regions.

articles.title: Leveraging leaf-level optimality processes with explicit acclimation improves global GPP representation in an individual-based DGVM (LPJ-GUESS v4.1.1)
articles.titleEn: Leveraging leaf-level optimality processes with explicit acclimation improves global GPP representation in an individual-based DGVM (LPJ-GUESS v4.1.1)
articles.abstract: Vegetation models are indispensable tools for investigating and projecting the terrestrial carbon cycle, both as standalone models and embedded in global climate models. However, current models vary widely in their representation of ecosystem processes and consequently in their projected future carbon dynamics. Eco-evolutionary optimality (EEO) approaches, which derive and test hypotheses about optimal plant behaviour under specific environmental conditions as a consequence of natural selection, have been proposed as a means to improve the reliability of vegetation models and the robustness of their future projections. Here we embed EEO-derived models for photosynthesis and leaf dark respiration, and their acclimation to changing conditions, into the widely used LPJ-GUESS vegetation model. We evaluated the simulated gross primary production (GPP) patterns against remotely-sensed GPP derived from sun-induced fluorescence and found that the EEO configurations improved the spatial distributions (a mean reduction in error of 15 % across gridcells) and global interannual variability (a mean reduction in error of 32 % after accounting for differences in global totals) compared to the standard version of LPJ-GUESS. Evaluation against GPP fluxes from eddy flux covariance measurements also showed improved performance, the R 2 of 5 d GPP increased from 0.45 to 0.48 (averaged across 147 sites). The simulated global carbon pools, fluxes, burnt area and biome distributions were not impacted substantially. The improvements were achieved with no alteration to processes except photosynthesis, respiration and plant water uptake, and with no recalibration or tuning. The EEO configuration also reduced model run time and eliminated the need for poorly-constrained PFT-dependent parameters governing the temperature response of photosynthesis. As well as being a tangible improvement to LPJ-GUESS, this study further confirms the usefulness of EEO approaches to improve global vegetation models.

articles.title: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
articles.titleEn: Global-scale meteorological-to-groundwater drought propagation and the drivers and patterns of multi-year groundwater drought
articles.abstract: Groundwater stores a third of all global freshwater and supports water supply, irrigation and ecosystems across the world. As such, groundwater drought can have wide-reaching financial, social and environmental impacts, particularly when drought events are prolonged or multi-year. Although recent work has made significant progress in understanding the drivers and patterns of multi-year meteorological droughts, we do not know how this signal translates into multi-year groundwater drought, where subsurface processes, anthropogenic influences and abstractions can alter the meteorological signal. This is particularly true at the global-scale, where a major barrier to understanding large-scale groundwater drought dynamics is the difficulty of obtaining consistent and comprehensive groundwater data. In this research, we use a new global hyper-resolution (∼1 km) groundwater dataset to investigate the global patterns and drivers of groundwater drought from 1960–2019, with a specific focus on multi-year events. We start by characterizing the propagation of meteorological (represented by SPEI-12) to groundwater drought, evaluating how and to what extent the sub-surface plays a role in modulating the meteorological drought signal. Subsequently, we define three global groundwater response types that provide a framework for understanding the processes and geo-physical drivers of normal versus multi-year groundwater droughts. We find that 35 % of global groundwater grid cells have an average groundwater drought duration which is multi-year. In 83 % of these locations, the subsurface extends the meteorological drought signal, whereas in the remaining 17 %, groundwater drought duration appears to be primarily driven by meteorological anomalies. Our analysis offers new insights into global-scale drought exposure by identifying regions which have been most vulnerable to multi-year groundwater drought in the past, as well as those which might be more vulnerable in the future. Importantly, our typology also highlights areas where multi-year groundwater droughts can be anticipated based on meteorological drought anomalies and can therefore inform strategies for managing and mitigating future water scarcity risks.

articles.title: Monthly-updated territorial fossil CO 2 emissions estimates for Japan
articles.titleEn: Monthly-updated territorial fossil CO 2 emissions estimates for Japan
articles.abstract: We present a low-lag, monthly dataset of emissions of carbon dioxide from fossil fuel consumption and industrial processes in Japan, derived directly from official activity data and starting in 2007. Such estimates will be crucial for near-real-time monitoring of emissions and making swift policy responses accordingly. When aggregated, our estimates replicate the annual data published through the UNFCCC national inventory report very well, with only small discrepancies which we describe and quantify. The dataset is produced with a lag of 2 months and can be used to estimate the annual emissions a year ahead of the official estimates submitted to the UNFCCC, and also provides a better starting point for short-term emissions projections. Data are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20023226 (Kunimitsu and Andrew, 2026).

articles.title: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
articles.titleEn: The Standardized Soil Moisture-Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI): daily scale global data set and event catalogue for compound dry-hot extremes (1961–2023)
articles.abstract: Compound dry-hot extremes (CDHEs) are among the most damaging climate hazards. Most metrics used to diagnose them are estimated at monthly or seasonal resolution or rely on precipitation-based drought proxies that can miss fast soil moisture-driven land–atmosphere feedbacks. This paper delivers two tightly linked products for global CDHE monitoring over land (excluding Antarctica) at 0.1° resolution for 1961–2023: (i) a continuous, daily severity index, i.e. the Standardized Soil Moisture–Temperature Compound Index (SSTCI), and (ii) a companion, event-based CDHE catalogue derived from SSTCI. SSTCI is constructed by first quantifying grid specific soil moisture memory using dry-down events, fitting an exponential decay to estimate a characteristic dry-down timescale ( τ ). This memory is used to compute a Standardized Antecedent Soil Moisture Index (SASMI), which is paired with a daily Standardized Temperature Index (STI). SASMI and STI are then integrated using a Frank copula to represent their joint probability, which is transformed to a standardized normal variate to yield SSTCI, providing a spatially comparable daily measure of compound dry-hot stress. To move from daily index values to physically interpretable hazards, we post-process the daily SSTCI series by discarding very short extreme spells and merging those separated by only brief interruptions, so that fragmented detections become single coherent events; the resulting catalogue carries event timing and magnitude descriptors suitable for event-based statistics. Our evaluation shows broad agreement between SASMI (SSTCI) and established drought (compound) metrics and vegetation stress. Moreover, SSTCI captures the timing and evolution of well documented CDHEs across multiple regions and timescales when applied to case studies. Together, the resulting SSTCI fields and event catalogue provide a consistent, daily scale foundation for global monitoring, process attribution of land–atmosphere feedback, and early-warning applications for compound dry-hot hazards. Data introduced in this paper are openly accessible from https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18280747 (SSTCI) (Aftab et al., 2026c) and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20826759 (CDHE event catalogue) (Aftab et al., 2026b).

articles.title: Divergent Patterns of Interactions Between Dissolved Organic Matter and Microbial Communities in Mangroves and Salt Marshes
articles.titleEn: Divergent Patterns of Interactions Between Dissolved Organic Matter and Microbial Communities in Mangroves and Salt Marshes
articles.abstract: Mangroves and salt marshes are major blue carbon reservoirs, where dissolved organic matter (DOM) dynamics are co‐regulated by primary production, microbial transformation, and environmental conditions. Understanding whether these two coastal wetlands exhibit fundamentally different DOM–microbe interaction patterns is critical for assessing blue carbon functioning. However, such interactions and their environmental determinants remain unclear. Here, we conduct a continental‐scale comparison between mangroves and salt marshes spanning ~5000 km of China's coastline to elucidate the linkages between DOM molecules and microbial communities. DOM and bacterial β‐diversity are positively correlated in both wetlands, but their respective distance–decay relationships are significant only in salt marshes. DOM–microbe co‐occurrence networks are bacteria‐dominated in both wetlands, but are more complex and positively linked in mangroves, whereas negatively linked in salt marshes. DOM‐gene networks show that carbon fixation and methanogenesis genes are primarily associated with recalcitrant DOM in mangroves, but with labile DOM in salt marshes. Soil pH, together with mean annual temperature, dissolved organic carbon, soil organic carbon, total nitrogen, and amorphous calcium, collectively influence the divergences in DOM composition, microbial community structure, and carbon metabolic functions. These findings offer key insights into DOM–microbe interaction mechanisms and their divergent patterns across “blue carbon” ecosystems.
